assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory predicted that a small twist angle flattens the moire bands of bilayer graphene, and experiment then found correlated insulators and superconductivity at the magic angle. This is a simple, general mechanism (band flattening by interference of two lattices) that opened a new field of tunable correlated matter, which is the kind of clean-model-meets-experiment result I value most.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model supplied the decisive theory and the Jarillo-Herrero group supplied the 2018 experimental discovery. The three names give a theory-plus-experiment configuration. Other groups (for example Dean, Yacoby, Young, Efetov) also contributed early confirmations and the supplied credit does not cover them.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups and platforms within a few years, and the interpretation of flat bands is stable. Recognition is timely, though the nature of the superconducting pairing is still debated.
uncertainties: Origin and symmetry of the superconducting state remain unsettled.

Early theoretical contributions beyond the credited names (for example Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell et al.) may deserve consideration; I cannot verify their relative priority from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal symmetry with spin-orbit coupling gives a new Z2 topological class of insulators, and the quantum spin Hall edge channels were observed in HgTe wells. It is a robust, universal, rigorously analysable concept that reshaped condensed matter theory and materials search.
assessment.attribution: Kane-Mele supplied the theoretical foundation and Molenkamp's group the first experimental demonstration (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposing HgTe, who are not in the credited list). Any fair prize must handle the BHZ and Zhang contribution and the 3D generalisation (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents), which are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed across HgTe, Bi-based materials and ARPES studies, and the concept is mature. The 2016 prize recognised related topological phases, so some may see this as partly covered, but the Z2 insulator is distinct.
uncertainties: Priority questions involving Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D theorists could complicate the three-person limit.
Overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize may reduce urgency.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock with magic-wavelength trapping reached 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, enabling relativistic geodesy-scale tests and a path to redefining the second. The idea is elegant and the performance gain is large and concrete.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye's group drove it to the lowest systematic uncertainties. Two names are a clean configuration, although Hall and Hansch frequency-comb work, already recognised in 2005, underlies it, and ion-clock work (Wineland, Rosenband) is a parallel line.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across several laboratories, and the field is mature. Timing is good because clocks are approaching redefinition of the second.
uncertainties: Competition with single-ion optical clocks for credit; the prize 2012 already honoured ion control.
Practical redefinition of the second has not yet happened.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture gives a unified, critical-like description of the rigidity transition in grains, foams and emulsions, with universal scaling and a minimal-model framework. This is the kind of simple general mechanism in disordered matter that statistical physics should honour, and it connects to learning landscapes and glassy systems.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram and then the point-J critical scaling with O'Hern, Silbert and Langer; Wyart, Zhang and others developed the theory of marginal stability. The two-name list is neat but omits collaborators and later theory, so the allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Supported by simulation, numerics and some experiments, but the exact universality class and the relation to glass physics remain debated. The theory is somewhat less settled than the winners above, so recognition could be slightly early.
uncertainties: Ongoing disagreement about dimensional dependence of critical exponents and whether jamming is a true phase transition.
The mean-field exact solution in infinite dimensions (Parisi, Zamponi and others) may be seen as the rigorous core by some.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type Hamiltonians with tunable parameters, giving quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter. This is a clean bridge between statistical physics models and experiment, and the superfluid-Mott transition and later many-body studies are landmarks.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical proposal (Jaksch, Bruder, Cirac, Gardiner, Zoller, 1998) and the experiment (Greiner, Mandel, Esslinger, Hansch, Bloch, 2002) divide credit among five or more people, so a three-person limit is a real constraint. I propose Zoller for theory and Bloch and Greiner for experiments, while noting Esslinger and Cirac as plausible alternatives.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced worldwide. BEC and cold-atom control already have prizes (1997, 2001), which moderates novelty, but quantum simulation is a distinct step.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Cirac, Esslinger, Bloch, Greiner and Zoller is unresolved.
Overlap with earlier BEC and laser-cooling prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube detected a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and later associated neutrinos with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opening neutrino astronomy at a new energy range. It required a km^3 detector in Antarctic ice and is of lasting importance.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Spiering was a key leader of the AMANDA and IceCube collaboration. Large-collaboration attribution is delicate; other pioneers (for example Learned, Markov, Roberts for DUMAND/Baikal ideas) are outside the supplied list. I take the two credited leaders.
assessment.maturity: Detection is statistically solid, but source identification is still limited to a few objects and the origin of the diffuse flux is not understood. Reasonably mature as an instrumentation and discovery achievement, but the astrophysical interpretation is still developing.
uncertainties: Origin of the bulk of the astrophysical neutrino flux is unknown.
Leadership credit within a thousand-person collaboration is hard to assign.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The multifractal and intermittency description of fully developed turbulence is a central problem in my own field, going back to Kolmogorov 1941 and its correction in 1962. Frisch and Parisi gave the multifractal formalism and Sreenivasan led the experimental measurements of scaling. Significance is high, but the work is better thought of as a long programme than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: Frisch and Parisi proposed the multifractal model, Benzi and collaborators the extended self-similarity, and Sreenivasan measured scaling exponents. Parisi is not credited here and Kolmogorov and Obukhov are the actual originators, so any prize would be partial and contested.
assessment.maturity: Experiments and simulations confirm anomalous scaling, but there is no first-principles derivation of the exponents from Navier-Stokes. This is exactly why I rank it below the more settled items.
uncertainties: No accepted analytical theory derives the intermittency exponents.
Credit for the multifractal formalism is incomplete because Parisi is absent from the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computation showed that large quantum computations are possible in principle despite noise, and the toric code linked this to topological order. These are deep and original ideas that now guide experimental devices.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane independently discovered the first quantum codes, Kitaev introduced topological codes and anyonic fault tolerance. Gottesman, Calderbank, Aharonov, Ben-Or, Knill, Laflamme and Preskill also made decisive contributions that the three-name list leaves out.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations of below-threshold logical qubits have appeared recently, but a scalable fault-tolerant machine does not exist yet. Recognition could be seen as timely or premature.
uncertainties: Whether this is physics or computer science for a physics prize.
Many equally decisive contributors are not in the credited names.
